vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pay-bills
Version: 0.0.4

The skill bundle is designed to interact with the CreditWithBleon API for payments and related services. It utilizes Node.js scripts to manage local state, specifically a persistent device ID (`.device_id`) and a session token (`.session_token`), both stored within the skill's own directory. All file system operations (read, write, delete) and network calls to `lodu.bleon.net` are directly aligned with the stated purpose of authentication and transaction processing. There is no evidence of prompt injection attempts in `skill.md` to subvert the agent, nor any malicious code for data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or persistence mechanisms beyond the skill's intended scope.

llm.summary: The skill’s code, instructions, and requested access are internally consistent with a Nigerian airtime/data purchase integration, but the package comes from an unknown source and stores session tokens locally—review the endpoint and files before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the behavior: SKILL.md documents an API for buying airtime/data and the included scripts generate trx/device IDs and manage a session token—these are expected for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to call the noted HTTPS API and run three small Node.js helper scripts that read/write files in the skill directory (.device_id, .session_token). That is within scope for a payment integration, but the instructions assume the runtime can execute node and persist files in the skill directory.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or downloads; helper scripts are bundled with the skill. No external installers or archived code are fetched at runtime, so install risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. It does persist sessionToken and deviceId as plaintext files in the skill directory which is proportional to the function but worth noting as sensitive data stored on disk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true and does not request system-wide config changes. It only reads/writes files in its own directory (session and device id), which is expected for its auth flow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and its small helper scripts are easy to read, but take these precautions before installing: (1) Verify the API endpoint (https://lodu.bleon.net) and confirm the service is legitimate—there's no homepage or known origin in the registry entry. (2) Understand that session tokens and device IDs are stored as plaintext files (.session_token, .device_id) in the skill directory; don't install in a sensitive or shared filesystem and consider deleting/clearing the token after use. (3) The runtime must be able to run node; review the three included JS files yourself (they are short and benign) before use. (4) When performing real purchases, verify transaction IDs and amounts, and avoid providing any unrelated credentials. (5) If you are uncomfortable with autonomous agent invocation, keep the skill user-invocable only and do not grant it broad autonomous permissions.
